name: std::advance

declarations.code:
template <class InputIt, class Distance>

void advance(InputIt &it, Distance n);

template <class InputIt, class Distance>

constexpr void advance(InputIt &it, Distance n);

intro:
Increments given iterator it by n elements.

If n is negative, the iterator is decremented. In this case, InputIt must meet the requirements of LegacyBidirectionalIterator, otherwise the behavior is undefined.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.text:
it

 -

 iterator to be advanced


 n

 -

 number of elements it should be advanced


 Type requirements


 -InputIt must meet the requirements of LegacyInputIterator.

sections.title: Complexity
sections.text:
Linear.

However, if InputIt additionally meets the requirements of LegacyRandomAccessIterator, complexity is constant.

sections.title: Notes
sections.text: The behavior is undefined if the specified sequence of increments or decrements would require that a non-incrementable iterator (such as the past-the-end iterator) is incremented, or that a non-decrementable iterator (such as the front iterator or the singular iterator) is decremented.
